Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1248 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE NORTHEAST...FROM CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA INTO NORTHWEST
NEBRASKA...AND FROM SOUTHERN KANSAS INTO NORTHWEST OKLAHOMA...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over small parts of the Great Plains,
and over the Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.
Isolated hail may occur with the Northern Plains activity.

...Central SD into northwest NE...
A shortwave trough will move southeastward across SK/MB, with at
least some influence extending southward across the northern Plains.
A surface trough will develop southward into central SD and western
NE, where strong heating will occur. A narrow band of uncapped
instability is forecast, with several models indicating scattered
storms late in the day. Southerly 850 mb winds over 20 kt will
aid/maintain moisture into the area, and forecast soundings show
marginally favorable hodographs for supercells. Localized hail may
occur initially, with some clustering and wind potential into the
early evening.

...Southern KS into northwest OK...
A surface trough/wind shift is forecast to exist from southern KS
into northern OK, with southerly winds and strong heating to the
south. Near/north of the boundary, winds will remain southeasterly
with higher dewpoints. General model consensus is for the deeply
mixed boundary layer to support an uncapped air mass, with a zone of
storms developing. These will likely produce strong outflow, and a
few severe gusts may occur.

...Northeast...
Southwest winds aloft will persist over the region as an upper high
remains over the Atlantic and a shortwave trough approaches the
Lower Great Lakes by late afternoon. Height tendencies will remain
neutral from NY into WV/VA during the day, but strong heating, PWAT
near 2.00" and sufficient MUCAPE should aid scattered storm
development near a weak surface trough after 19Z. This would include
from south-central NY into central PA and across the higher terrain
of western VA. A few strong gusts cannot be ruled out.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0234 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over parts of the Northeast and Upper
Mississippi Valley region on Friday. Locally strong wind gusts
appear most likely.

...Northeast...
Beneath modest southwest winds aloft, a large area of thunderstorms
is likely Friday afternoon from the TN Valley/Appalachians into the
Northeast, as daytime heating combines with a moist air mass and
marginal instability. General thunderstorm activity appears most
likely across these areas given weak winds at or below 20 kt below
700 mb. However, increasing daytime storm coverage could produce
locally gusty winds/outflows, especially where pockets of greater
instability develop with the higher dewpoints over eastern areas.

...WI/MN/IA...
A northwest flow regime over the northern Plains will gradually move
toward the Upper Great Lakes Friday into Saturday, with cooling
temperatures aloft and 500 mb winds on the order of 30-35 kt. A weak
surface trough may develop from Lake Superior southwestward into IA
during the day, with eventual destabilization as southwest winds at
850 mb increase to around 20 kt. Shear will not be particularly
strong, but storms are likely late in the day into the overnight
from WI into IA. While isolated severe gusts or hail cannot be ruled
out, predictability issues preclude adding a risk area at this time.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 081200Z - 131200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Saturday/D4...
Southwest midlevel winds of only 25 kt will exist across the
Northeast, while low-level moisture remains in place supporting up
to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE with poor lapse rates aloft. This will support
daytime thunderstorms over a large area from the Appalachians into
the Northeast, and a few severe gusts cannot be ruled out.
Otherwise, normal gusty outflow winds are to be expected.

To the west, an area of stronger instability is forecast across the
Mid MO Valley, where northwesterly midlevel winds of 35 kt will
exist along the southern periphery of a trough sweeping across the
Upper Great Lakes. Evening/overnight storms may occur across parts
of eastern NE, IA, and MO, and instability may be large enough to
warrant at least low severe probabilities as the event nears in
time.

...Sunday/D5...
Drying will occur aloft over parts of the Northeast as a wave moves
into Quebec, but substantial low-level moisture will still support
scattered thunderstorms ahead of a cold front across the Mid
Atlantic. Shear will again be weak, but perhaps enough mean wind
speeds will exist for storms to be mobile/produce areas of strong
gusts.

To the west, low-level moisture is forecast to shift a bit farther
north into the Dakotas, and this will occur beneath stronger
northwest flow aloft. This area bears watching in later outlooks, as
wind profiles may somewhat favor supercells. Predictability is
currently low.

...Mon/D6 to Wed/D8...
While predictability decreases further during this time frame,
moderate west to northwest flow aloft will remain from the upper MS
Valley across the Great Lakes, which will spread into the Northeast
D7/D8. If a wave does amplify within this flow regime, a corridor of
damaging winds could develop given upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints
along/south of the mean frontal zone (roughly IA to NY/PA by end of
the period). Model variation is currently too great to depict an
precise corridor.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0745 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 051300Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS...AND SOUTHEASTERN
ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible today across the mid 
Mississippi Valley.  Isolated severe gusts may also occur in parts
of the southern High Plains, and in southeastern Arizona.

...Mid Mississippi Valley...
Water-vapor imagery this morning shows a broad upper trough over the
north-central U.S. with a couple of embedded disturbances.  A
leading weak impulse appears associated with a small cluster of
strong to locally severe activity early this morning across the
IA-MO border vicinity, near and immediately north of a stationary
front.  These showers/thunderstorms will likely continue east of the
MS River but it remains unclear whether these storms maintain a
localized risk for severe before gradually weakening.  Later today,
ascent associated with an upstream disturbance moving through the
base of the larger-scale trough over NE into IA, will favor
additional storm development as the boundary layer heats south of
the frontal zone.  Moderate buoyancy is forecast by guidance and
sufficient deep-layer shear will support some potential storm
organization.  The stronger storms may yield an episodic severe risk
before gradually diminishing during the evening.  

...Southeastern Arizona...
A seasonably moist airmass sampled this morning by surface
observations (lower 60s F dewpoints) will undergo strong heating
through late afternoon.  Orographic lifting will favor convection
developing over the higher terrain and gradually
spreading/developing into the lower deserts during the early
evening.  Very steep low to mid-level lapse rates will contribute
towards a risk for strong downdrafts capable of a microburst threat
(60-80 mph).  Considered a Slight-Risk based on potentially
scattered storm coverage moving into the lower deserts, but
sufficient model run-to-run (time-lagged HRRR) variability and model
ensemble spread (i.e., 00z HREF vs. REFS) preclude a wind-driven
upgrade at this time.

...Southern High Plains...
Weak but adequately moist, post-frontal upslope flow into the Raton
Mesa vicinity will favor widely scattered diurnal storm development
by mid-late afternoon.  Modest west-northwesterly mid-level flow
will favor storms and their incipient outflow to the east-southeast
into the adjacent High Plains.  Given the steep lapse rates and
relatively dry sub-cloud layer, evaporative cooling will probably
result in a few storms being capable of localized severe gusts
(60-80 mph).

..Smith/Bentley.. 08/05/2026
